sentences.text:
This petition under Article 226 of the Constitution of India has been filed seeking the following relief(s):-
i) It is, therefore, prayed that this Hon'ble court may kindly be pleased to issue direction to the respondents to get construction of houses started of the petitioners in their allotted plots by providing police protection.
ii) To direct the respondents to complete reproceeding u/s 6 of Land Acquisition Act regarding rehabilitation of the petitioners without causing any further delay.
iii) To call for entire relevant record for kind perusal of this Hon'ble court.
iv) To grant any other relief which may deem fit and proper in the facts and circumstances of the case.
2. This petition is filed by helpless persons who have suffered displacement not only on account of Ban Sagar Dam Project but they have been denied the alternative sites on account of issuance of vague notifications under Sections 4 and 6 of the Land Acquisition Act.

3. It is submitted by the counsel for petitioners that after their displacement on account of submergence of their lands under the Ban Sagar Dam Project they were granted alternative sites in village Turki.

The notifications issued under Section 4 and 6 of the Land Acquisition Act for allotment of alternative sites to the displaced families were challenged by the owners of the said lands by filing W.P.No.8593/2006 and W.P.No.8594/2006, which was allowed by a Coordinate Bench of this Court by order dated 29.1.2007.
4.
It is submitted that thereafter the respondents have issued another notification dated 11.01.2008 under Section 4 of the Land Acquisition Act.

Since the land of village Turki was acquired, therefore,
the petitioners were granted alternative sites.
The possession was delivered.

The petitioners started raising constructions but on account of the fact that the notification issued under Sections 4 and 6 of the Land Acquisition Act were quashed, the construction raised by the petitioners was demolished and again they have been rendered homeless.

5. Now, the respondents have issued a notification under Section 4 of the Land Acquisition Act on 11.01.2008 but the final notification under Section 6 of the Land Acquisition Act is not being issued and, therefore, this petition was filed.

6. Considered the submissions made by counsel for the petitioners.
7.

It is not out of place to mention here that notification under Section 4 of the Land Acquisition Act issued on 11.01.2008 was challenged by the owners of the said land by filing W.P.No.3219/2008 and W.P.No.3220/2008.

By interim orders dated 14.03.2008 passed in W.P.No.3219/2008 and Gaya Prasad vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/114857735/
3 W.P.No.3220/2008 the operation of the impugned notification dated 11.01.2008 was stayed.

entities.text: Gaya Prasad vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Thus,
it is clear that on account of interim order passed in W.P.No.3219/2008 and W.P.No.3220/2008 notification issued under Section 6 of the Land Acquisition Act could not be passed.

8. Today, by a separate order passed in W.P.No.3219/2008 and W.P.No.3220/2008, the notification dated 11.01.2008 has been quashed with a direction to the respondents to issue a fresh notification for acquisition by specifically giving the details for identification of the land, as already directed by a coordinate Bench of this Court in W.P.No.8593/2006 (Pramod Kumar Gupta and others vs. State of M.P. and others).
9.

entities.text: Pramod Kumar Gupta and others vs. State of M.P. and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the present case also the petitioners have sought a direction for the respondents to issue a final notification and in view of the order passed by this Court in W.P.No.3219/2008 and W.P.No.3220/2008 the relief sought by the petitioners has rendered infructuous.
10. So far as the interim relief which was sought by the petitioners is concerned, it appears that no interim order was passed thereby protecting the possession of the petitioners.
It is submitted by counsel for petitioners they were dispossessed after demolition of their belongings.
11. Under these circumstances, in absence of any prayer for grant of any compensation, no further relief can be granted to the petitioners.
However a liberty is granted to the petitioners that in case if they so desire then they can file a fresh writ petition or may file a civil suit for grant of compensation.
12. With aforesaid observation, the petition is finally disposed of.
(G.S. AHLUWALIA) JUDGE HEMANT SARAF 2024.02.05 19:06:01 +05'30'
